feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: FrameForge: Harnessing Priors of Video Foundation Models for Unified Image Generation
entry.summary:
FrameForge leverages video foundation models for unified conditional image generation by using input-adaptive virtual temporal relations to model diverse condition-target transformations.

Why it matters: It improves unified image generation and editing quality by repurposing video models' temporal dynamics without restricting tasks to fixed temporal positions.

entry.title: Does Scaling Toward AGI Depend on What System-1 Lets System-2 Execute?
entry.summary:
Researchers propose a predict-gate-execute-update loop where a lightweight System-1 gates execution to optimize System-2 compute scaling.

Why it matters: Filtering low-utility candidates prior to execution reduces the massive compute costs required for scaling System-2 reasoning and agentic tool use.

entry.title: Apriel Voice 27B Preview: An Open Model for Speech, Reasoning, and Tool Use
entry.summary:
Apriel Voice 27B Preview is an open speech-language model built on Gemma 4 26B-A4B that unifies direct speech processing, multimodal inputs, reasoning, and tool use within a shared backbone.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that a single open model can natively handle speech understanding, complex reasoning, and tool calls without relying on a separate pipeline dialogue model.

entry.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
entry.summary:
The Latent Reasoning in Continuous space (LARC) framework enables unified multimodal models to reason over continuous hidden states rather than discrete tokens, improving test-time scaling for image generation.

Why it matters: By replacing discrete text chains-of-thought with continuous latent reasoning, unified multimodal models gain test-time scaling and superior compositional control during text-to-image generation.

entry.title: Wizard: Manipulate Any World in Real Time via Agentic Control
entry.summary:
Wizard is an agentic game world model that enables real-time, fine-grained control over character motions with zero-shot generalization across novel scenes, characters, and actions.

Why it matters: It decouples explicit game logic from visual generation, allowing player-driven creation of interactive virtual worlds with consistent mechanics and real-time control without needing scene-specific retraining.

entry.title: HiFOR: Hierarchical Foresight with Action-Guided World Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Model
entry.summary:
HiFOR is a hierarchical foresight framework for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models that uses action-guided world grounding and dependency masking to unify short-term, milestone, and long-term future predictions for robotic action generation.

Why it matters: It improves robotic manipulation policies by explicitly grounding action generation in relevant multi-horizon temporal predictions rather than treating short-term dynamics and long-term goals separately.

entry.title: Venus-DefakerOne2: A Vision-Forensics Foundation Model with Broader Coverage
entry.summary:
Venus-DefakerOne2 is a vision-forensics foundation model trained on tens of millions of samples to detect digital manipulations and physical spoofs across both images and videos.

Why it matters: It establishes a single, highly accurate foundation model capable of handling diverse media types and forgery threats that previously required separate expert models.

entry.title: ReLift: Dense 3D Tracking as Lifted Trajectory Repair
entry.summary:
ReLift recasts monocular dense 3D tracking as a decoupled, feed-forward trajectory repair and completion task using geometric attention mechanisms.

Why it matters: It creates a reusable trajectory refinement module that improves 3D tracking accuracy across various base models and automatically scales with future advances in 2D trackers and 3D geometry providers.

entry.title: No Channels Left Behind: Understanding Diffusion Acceleration through Residual Gates
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that diffusion model training acceleration stems from the reorganization of the AdaLN-Zero residual gate α, introducing a teacher-free radial objective that improves generation by broadening channel-wise gate participation.

Why it matters: Identifying residual-gate reorganization as a primary driver of diffusion acceleration enables lightweight, teacher-free regularization techniques that speed up training and boost image quality without complex auxiliary pipelines.

entry.title: CaPtain: A Pipeline for Post-Training Code-as-Policy Robot Agents
entry.summary:
CaPtain is an open post-training pipeline for Code-as-Policy robot agents that uses SFT and multi-turn RL with a privileged physical critic to fine-tune small vision-language models without relying on frontier models or VLAs at test time.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that small, open-weights vision-language models can outperform frontier models on robot manipulation tasks via post-training without relying on closed APIs or privileged state during deployment.

entry.title: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated ten visual foundation models across four spatial capability levels using frozen-feature probes on streaming egocentric indoor video to assess spatial state maintenance and update under self-motion.

Why it matters: The findings show that static visual decoding performance is insufficient for spatial tasks, requiring visual foundation models to be explicitly evaluated on persistent, predictive, and action-guiding spatial representations.

entry.title: WorldBridge: Bridging Video and Action for Task Generalization in World Action Models
entry.summary:
WorldBridge is a World Action Model (WAM) that decouples video and action prediction into separate experts linked via structured attention and trained using joint flow matching to improve robot task generalization.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that leveraging broad action-free video data combined with minimal action supervision significantly enhances a robot's ability to generalize to unseen physical manipulation tasks.

entry.title: REA: A Routed Embodied Agent Runtime for Asynchronous Brain-Cerebellum Control
entry.summary:
REA is a unified embodied agent runtime that orchestrates deliberative System 2 reasoning, an embodied router, and reactive System 0 policies without forcing running fast policies to wait on the slow brain model.

Why it matters: It enables asynchronous, hybrid control in robotics by successfully pairing slow, highly generalizable foundation models with fast, fine-grained policies without incurring latency bottlenecks.

entry.title: On the Origin and Evolution of Training-Inference Mismatch in LLM Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Researchers formalize LLM RL training-inference mismatch into numerical discrepancy and policy lag, introducing Discrepancy-Lag Correction (DLC) to stabilize training by removing prefix bias and resynchronizing when effective sample size drops below 0.5.

Why it matters: DLC prevents training collapses in asynchronous RL for LLMs caused by off-policy weight staleness and engine numerical differences, which standard per-token corrections fail to catch.

entry.title: WeFair: Fidelity-Aware Alignment from Human Feedback for Personalized Query Rewriting in Short-Video Search
entry.summary:
WeFair presents a three-stage, fidelity-aware feedback alignment framework for personalized short-video query rewriting that uses intent verification to prevent intent drift caused by consumption-behavioral feedback.

Why it matters: It demonstrates how to align compact LLM query rewriters using a structured fidelity curriculum to optimize engagement without sacrificing historical intent accuracy in high-throughput search engines.

entry.title: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention
entry.summary:
Latent Sparse Attention (LSA) achieves subquadratic long-context processing by hierarchically clustering keys in a learned latent space and scoring cluster hierarchies rather than individual keys.

Why it matters: LSA enables computationally efficient prefill, decode, and training for ultra-long context windows up to 10M tokens without sacrificing model accuracy.

entry.title: ACCT: Asymmetric Cross-LLM Context Transfer
entry.summary:
ACCT enables asymmetric cross-model context transfer by converting a source LLM's KV cache into a sparse KV state directly consumable by a target LLM, skipping target prefill.

Why it matters: Heterogeneous LLM deployments can reuse context prefill computations across different model scales, dramatically reducing computational costs and latency.

entry.title: Subquadratic Attention with a Hierarchical Tree-Structured Indexer
entry.summary:
Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA) achieves asymptotically subquadratic attention scaling by using a hierarchical, tree-structured indexer that routes queries top-down through recursively compressed key summaries.

Why it matters: It enables large language models to process extreme context lengths beyond one million tokens without incurring the prohibitive quadratic scaling costs of standard attention.

entry.title: CRoS: Causality Reward on Scrambled CoTs Improves Accuracy and Reasoning Faithfulness
entry.summary:
CRoS improves LLM reasoning by using a new causality reward that scrambles CoT step order without altering step content, preventing unfaithful reasoning induced by step deletion or error injection.

Why it matters: CRoS provides a training reward that ensures Chain-of-Thought steps causally drive the final output without degrading model exploration or inducing uninformative reasoning.

entry.title: There Is No Free Loop: When Does Looping a Trained Model Pay for Its Inference Compute?
entry.summary:
Adding layer loops post-pretraining only pays for its inference compute cost in small models (0.8B), failing to outperform unlooped baselines at 4B and 9B scales.

Why it matters: Inserting architectural loops after pretraining is inefficient for scaling performance in larger models compared to simple unlooped baselines under equal compute constraints.

entry.title: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training for Prompt Injection Security
entry.summary:
SecPO introduces a novel preference loss function and an efficient adversarial training pipeline (best@240) to drastically reduce prompt injection attack success rates without degrading benign model utility.

Why it matters: SecPO provides a theoretically principled method to robustly defend LLM agents against severe prompt injection attacks while retaining performance on standard benign tasks.

entry.title: DAMI: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization for Enhanced Long-Context Retrieval in Gated Linear Attention
entry.summary:
Dual-Axis Memory Initialization (DAMI) sets non-trainable decay and gate parameters in gated linear attention models to improve long-context retrieval.

Why it matters: It improves long-context retrieval in linear attention models through pre-training parameter initialization without adding parameters or sacrificing language modeling accuracy.

entry.title: Optimizing Stochastic Policy Geometry for Few-Step Flow Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Geo-FSRL optimizes stochastic policy geometry for few-step flow reinforcement learning by selecting the coefficient-preserving Gaussian policy that minimizes conditional KL divergence induced by velocity-output updates.

Why it matters: It improves reinforcement learning performance for few-step diffusion and flow models without altering the original deterministic inference pipeline or requiring additional sampling steps.

entry.title: Dynamical Memory Transformer: Selective Recurrent Memories with Constant Cost Attention
entry.summary:
The Dynamical Memory Transformer (DMT) decouples sequence encoding from reading by using parallel dynamical memory units with constant-cost attention, avoiding KV-cache growth.

Why it matters: DMT enables constant-memory autoregressive inference and sub-quadratic training while retaining strong attention-based memory retrieval and length extrapolation capabilities.

entry.title: TSBPO: Tree-Structured Branching for Policy Optimization in Interactive Language Agents
entry.summary:
TSBPO is a tree-structured sampling-to-update paradigm for interactive language agents that optimizes continuation allocation, multi-level advantage estimation, and multi-token loss aggregation in a single loop.

Why it matters: TSBPO improves policy optimization for interactive agents by resolving reward credit assignment and token loss aggregation without relying on response-length averaging.

entry.title: FDSML: Formula-Driven Supervised Metric Learning with Parameter-Aware Triplet Loss
entry.summary:
FDSML introduces formula-driven metric learning by replacing discrete class labels with parameter-space distance metrics to pre-train vision models without real images.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that leveraging continuous generative parameter spaces for relational supervision produces stronger, more transferrable representations than label-based classification when pre-training on synthetic mathematical data.

entry.title: On the Fundamental Limits of Prefill-Based Decoding Length Prediction
entry.summary:
Researchers derive fundamental theoretical bounds on prefill-based LLM decode length prediction, demonstrating that decoding stochasticity creates a hard performance ceiling where system error dominates model error.

Why it matters: Inference schedulers cannot overcome decode-length prediction errors caused by sampling noise, necessitating standardized benchmarks that evaluate predictors relative to theoretical limits rather than absolute metrics.

entry.title: Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker
entry.summary:
Glance unifies reranking and generation within a single LLM backbone using lightweight decision adapters and pointer heads, scoring candidate passages from a shared prefill without separate query-passage processing.

Why it matters: Eliminating dedicated reranker models reduces serving complexity and memory redundancy while outperforming standalone cross-encoders through shared context caching.

entry.title: Don't Lose the Thread: Empowering Long-Horizon LLM Agents with Cognitive Resource Self-Allocation
entry.summary:
CORAL enables LLM agents to manage context via a working memory toolset that checkpoints progress and resets context, reducing input tokens 6-7x while boosting long-horizon task accuracy.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that active working memory management significantly cuts LLM inference costs while preventing cognitive overload in long-horizon reasoning tasks.

entry.title: One Vector or Many? Clustered Optimal-Transport Steering under Quantization
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated clustered optimal-transport activation steering against Difference of Means (DiM) for toxicity mitigation, finding token-fitted variants outperform DiM even under INT8 and NF4 quantization.

Why it matters: Token-specific clustered steering provides stronger toxicity reduction than single-vector methods without requiring retraining when transferring to quantized NF4 or INT8 models.

entry.title: Rethinking Pre-pretraining
entry.summary:
Compute-matched synthetic pre-pretraining fails to beat pure natural-language training across data regimes, with prior reported gains largely driven by suboptimal weight initialization.

Why it matters: Allocating dedicated compute budgets to synthetic pre-pretraining stages is ineffective compared to directly training or repeating epochs on natural language.

entry.title: Tokenizer Tokens Tell Training Tales
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizers leak dataset membership through rare tokens, introducing the RTAM-Fusion framework to outperform Vocabulary Overlap baselines using fewer shadow tokenizers.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that pre-trained BPE tokenizers expose training data privacy risks and that current membership defenses are insufficient against targeted adaptive attacks.

entry.title: Attention, Dynamic Wave and Hybrid Sequence Mixers in Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers formalize a Dynamic Wave recurrent layer and show a Hybrid Wave-Attention architecture achieves superior perplexity (5.95) over Pure Transformer (6.93) and Pure Wave (7.26) models at 10.94M parameters.

Why it matters: Claims of efficiency gains in non-attention sequence mixers depend heavily on the baseline implementation and backend used, making architectural hybridization primarily justifiable for perplexity improvements rather than memory savings.

entry.title: KV Cache Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce TRACE and dLLM-KVQ to address KV cache quantization in diffusion language models, accounting for cache-reuse errors caused by changing bidirectional token representations across denoising steps.

Why it matters: This work enables low-bit KV cache quantization for diffusion language models without suffering severe performance degraded by dynamic, non-causal token state updates.

entry.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
entry.summary:
SpecSlot is a pixel-space rectified-flow Transformer that decouples spectral detail from global attention sequence length by assigning DCT frequency bands to local slots and routing only low-frequency slots globally.

Why it matters: It enables pixel-space generative Transformers to scale up fine spectral detail without incurring the quadratic computational cost of long global attention sequences.

entry.title: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
entry.summary:
A probing framework evaluates ten visual foundation models across four spatial capability levels, revealing that strong visible-scene decoding does not guarantee object persistence, accurate feature prediction, or actionable goal-directed control.

Why it matters: Evaluating visual foundation models solely on current-frame decodability is insufficient for robotics, as spatial representations must persistently track unseen space and reliably update under motion for action.

entry.title: When to Assist and What to Suggest: Joint Gating and Memory-Grounded Hint Generation in One Compact Decoder
entry.summary:
A single 1B decoder unifies proactive hint timing and generation by gating from an intermediate layer, matching two-model pipelines with up to 1.76x less wall-clock time.

Why it matters: Consolidating proactive gating and generation into a single compact decoder significantly lowers latency and compute requirements without sacrificing end-to-end hint performance.

entry.title: Pre-Crime for Agents, at the Last Second: Probing When a Recruited Agent Gives In
entry.summary:
Linear probes on AI agent activations can detect when a multi-agent target is about to leak secrets to a peer prior to generating output, outperforming zero-shot decision-model monitors.

Why it matters: Pre-generation warnings allow overseers to intercept compromised AI agents before secret leaks trigger broader recruitment or collusion across multi-agent systems.

entry.title: VeriCUA: Verification as Agentic Exploration for Computer-Using Agents
entry.summary:
VeriCUA is a platform-agnostic framework that treats computer-using agent task verification as dynamic, agentic exploration using GUI and code checks to gather evidence.

Why it matters: It provides a unified, cross-platform approach to accurately verify agent task completion, improving data curation, benchmark evaluation, and reinforcement learning.

entry.title: How I Aligned Your Model: Scaling Up Multilingual Safety Training with Templates
entry.summary:
Researchers created a template-based pipeline and the resulting MSafeTemp dataset spanning 60 languages to scale up culturally localized multilingual safety alignment for LLMs.

Why it matters: Using template-augmented data like MSafeTemp improves multilingual model refusal capabilities and safety performance across underrepresented languages and region-specific harmful topics.

entry.title: Algebraic World Model: From Exploration to Proofs
entry.summary:
The Algebraic World Model (AWM) converts interactions with unfamiliar environments into executable Python hypotheses, simplifies them via category theory, and formalizes them in Lean 4 to generate machine-checkable proofs of reachability and impossibility.

Why it matters: AWM enables AI to autonomously construct interpretable, formal mathematical models of unknown environments, allowing kernel-verified proofs of system limits and impossibility without relying on predefined specifications.

entry.title: Prefix Executability: Evaluating Tool-Using Agents Beyond Final Success
entry.summary:
A new evaluation protocol called prefix executability assesses tool-using agents by measuring whether every prefix in a tool-call trajectory remains executable under schema constraints, state preconditions, and data dependencies.

Why it matters: Evaluating agents solely on final task success masks invalid intermediate steps, whereas prefix executability provides diagnostic metrics to detect trajectory failures and validate agent reliability.

entry.title: Retrieving from Your Own Mistakes: On-Policy Training of Embedding Models for Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entry.summary:
A new on-policy state training method for chain embedding retrievers trains encoders on self-generated retrieval states—including their own past mistakes—improving multi-hop evidence retrieval without requiring language model calls.

Why it matters: It enables lightweight, non-LLM embedding retrievers to robustly recover from early retrieval errors during multi-hop reasoning, closing the performance gap with complex search agents.

entry.title: Beyond Selected Breakthroughs: Evaluating Language Models on Randomly Sampled Mathematical Conjectures
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced OpenConjecture, a dataset of mathematical conjectures from post-February 2026 arXiv papers, to systematically evaluate frontier GPT models on a random sample of 200 open problems without problem-specific guidance.

Why it matters: Evaluating LLMs on unbiased, randomly sampled open conjectures reveals that assessing AI mathematical contributions requires evaluating statement fidelity, attribution, and novelty rather than relying solely on correctness.

entry.title: A Unified Hessian-Guided Framework for Post-Training Quantization
entry.summary:
A new post-training quantization framework uses a tractable Fisher-Hessian approximation to jointly optimize quantization ranges, linear transformations, and weight rounding under a unified output-sensitivity objective.

Why it matters: It enables higher accuracy LLM compression by accounting for task-level output sensitivity during low-bit quantization without incurring intractable computational costs.

entry.title: Only Accepted Tokens Count: An Energy Accounting of Speculative Decoding Under Latency Targets
entry.summary:
A benchmark of speculative decoding under production conditions reveals that energy savings depend heavily on acceptance rates, shrinking as batch size increases and turning into energy losses at large batches or low acceptance.

Why it matters: Using speculative decoding to meet strict latency targets can unexpectedly increase total energy consumption per token in high-throughput, batched production environments.

entry.title: Neighborhood Elites: Quality-Diversity Search for Uncertainty Quantification in Question Answering
entry.summary:
Neighborhood Elites (NE) uses Quality-Diversity search to construct input perturbation sets across edit types and answer explicitness, improving LLM uncertainty quantification for question answering.

Why it matters: By replacing unguided or generic input paraphrasing with structured QD search, LLMs can more reliably detect their own incorrect answers before downstream errors compound.

entry.title: Locating and Closing Information Gaps in Multi-Agent Systems
entry.summary:
SPLICE locates information gaps in multi-agent workflows, dynamically inserts directed communication edges, and uses a process-feature trained selector to decide whether to adopt candidate answer updates.

Why it matters: It prevents fixed multi-agent workflows from failing due to isolated evidence while using process-based validation to avoid downstream error propagation.

entry.title: world2vec: Mechanistic world models through latent dynamics learning
entry.summary:
World2vec learns reward-free mechanistic world models from observations and actions, matching or exceeding baseline control and system identification performance while using at least ten times fewer parameters.

Why it matters: By accurately capturing true system dynamics with high parameter efficiency, world2vec makes world models useful for mechanistic interpretability and scientific discovery rather than just task control.

entry.title: Discovering Interpretable Acoustic Features in Autoregressive Voice-Cloning TTS Models
entry.summary:
Researchers developed a feature-based interpretability framework using SAEs, PCA, and random directions to probe, steer, and automatically label latent acoustic concepts in autoregressive voice-cloning TTS models.

Why it matters: It establishes mechanistic methods to analyze, isolate, and control fine-grained acoustic and speaker characteristics inside autoregressive text-to-speech models.

entry.title: Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities
entry.summary:
Youtu-Parsing-Omni is a 5B-parameter omni-modal parser using a single encoder and unified schema to parse and temporally align text, audio, image, and video data into structured records.

Why it matters: It establishes a unified perception layer that allows AI agents to read, locate, and cite multimodal evidence across documents, audio, and video using a single architecture.

entry.title: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs
entry.summary:
Researchers proved the Platonic Representation Theorem for Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) and showed that positive view choice, rather than scale alone, drives cross-modal representation alignment.

Why it matters: Using JEPAs with high-quality positive views offers a mathematically proven, sample-efficient alternative to scaling language models for cross-modal alignment.

entry.title: Multi-Token Prediction Done Right
entry.summary:
Soft-MTP fixes a flaw in standard Multi-Token Prediction training by isolating the useful KL self-distillation signal from a noisy gradient residual using a straight-through gradient-routing trick.

Why it matters: Soft-MTP provides a zero-overhead, parameter-free optimization fix for multi-token pre-training that improves downstream reasoning capabilities and speculative decoding speed.

entry.title: Investor's Last Exam: Can AI Agents Do Equity Investment Without Seeing the Future?
entry.summary:
Investor's Last Exam (ILE) is a novel equity-research benchmark built on a timestamp-validated financial database to evaluate AI agents across complete financial analytical workflows without lookahead bias.

Why it matters: ILE establishes a diagnostic, point-in-time benchmark that pinpoints exact failures in the evidence-assumption-judgment chain of financial AI models.

entry.title: SO-101 Bench: Accessible Spatial Manipulation
entry.summary:
SO-101 Bench is a simulated Isaac Lab digital twin for language-conditioned spatial manipulation that perfectly correlates with real-world physical robot rankings (Spearman rho = 1.00).

Why it matters: It provides a zero-real-data evaluation pipeline for low-cost arms that accurately predicts real-world physical performance across complex spatial tasks.

entry.title: Online Dense Reinforcement Learning with Planning-Grounding Agent for UI Navigation on Live IOS Apps
entry.summary:
A novel online reinforcement learning framework trains UI navigation agents on live iOS apps by decoupling planning and UI grounding, using step-level LLM-as-a-Judge rewards and neighbor-conditioned value estimation via GiGPPO.

Why it matters: This approach enables smaller, lower-cost models to reliably navigate live mobile interfaces and recover from errors without relying on expensive frontier LLMs.

entry.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
entry.summary:
A new framework unifies pretraining, midtraining, SFT, and RL into a single likelihood-based algorithm by deriving RL objectives as maximum-likelihood fitting to model-generated target distributions.

Why it matters: Simplifies training infrastructure and improves efficiency by replacing complex multi-stage algorithmic pipelines with a single unified trainer.

entry.title: AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers
entry.summary:
AB-Attention is a training-free sparse attention method that accelerates Video Diffusion Transformers via local query clustering, probability-weighted block sampling, and fine-grained GPU tensor-core tile gathering.

Why it matters: It enables significantly faster video diffusion generation at high sparsity levels without degrading visual fidelity or requiring costly retraining.

entry.title: OpenFlyV2: An onboard vision-language-action model for aerial perception and navigation
entry.summary:
OpenFlyV2 is a unified vision-language-action model that performs onboard spatial reasoning, semantic perception, and continuous aerial control at 10 Hz on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX.

Why it matters: It proves that unified vision-language reasoning and real-time closed-loop flight control can run fully onboard edge hardware without relying on offboard computation.

entry.title: Matched Capabilities, Different Behaviors: A Controlled Study of MCP and CLI Interfaces for Language Agents
entry.summary:
The MICA framework reveals that exposing identical capabilities via Model Context Protocol versus CLI alters agent behavior, prompting the DART method to repair interface realizations and boost performance.

Why it matters: Interface representation directly dictates language agent behavior, meaning optimizing tool interfaces like MCP and CLI can significantly improve task success and reduce token overhead without altering core model capabilities.

entry.title: Broken on Arrival: Non-Functional Quantized LLM Artifacts in Public Model Registries and How to Catch Them
entry.summary:
An audit of public model registries revealed that 2.3% of official Ollama GGUF tags are non-functional low-bit quantizations, which can be fixed by applying importance matrix calibration during quantization.

Why it matters: Registries must functionally screen and calibrate low-bit quantized LLMs before publication to prevent distributing broken model artifacts to users.

entry.title: EPSBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Earnings Forecasting
entry.summary:
EPSBench evaluates LLM agents on quarterly earnings forecasting across 149 US firm-quarters by combining cited income-statement driver estimates with a deterministic accounting calculator.

Why it matters: The benchmark provides a standardized framework to isolate whether financial forecasting errors stem from underlying model assumptions or accounting arithmetic.

entry.title: Unlocking Any-Order Generation in Pretrained Autoregressive Image Models
entry.summary:
A new recipe adapts pretrained raster-scan autoregressive image models into any-order generators using future-aware positional embeddings and an ordering curriculum at 13-33% additional compute cost.

Why it matters: It enables complex image editing, inpainting, and outpainting in existing autoregressive models without requiring expensive from-scratch training on randomized token orderings.

entry.title: Weaken to Strengthen: Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Reasoning Models
entry.summary:
Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation (WISD) enhances large reasoning models on unlabeled prompts by using contrastive training signals from intentionally weakened counterparts created via quantization or pruning.

Why it matters: WISD enables effective post-training performance gains for reasoning models using only unlabeled prompts, removing reliance on stronger external teacher models or privileged data.

entry.title: Scaling Lean Theorem Proving for Real-World Code Verification
entry.summary:
EasyProver is a Lean proving system using recursive agents and elastic elaboration that, combined with the new real-world code verification benchmark Aegis, achieves high performance without model retraining.

Why it matters: It advances automated formal verification by demonstrating that off-the-shelf frontier models can scale to handle complex, implementation-level software verification tasks.

entry.title: TextSeal2: Distortion-Free LLM Watermarking with Copula Mixing and Memoryless Races
entry.summary:
TextSeal2 is a distortion-free LLM watermarking method that uses Gaussian copula key merging and memoryless exponential races to preserve output diversity, inference latency, and detection strength during speculative decoding.

Why it matters: It enables robust, zero-latency LLM text watermarking that remains intact and undetected in quality loss even when using draft-rejection speculative decoding acceleration.

entry.title: Retrieval as Traversal: Value-Indexed Memory for Stateful Long-Context Agents
entry.summary:
A stateful memory architecture frames retrieval as persistent local traversal through a value-indexed address space, regularized by information gain versus retrieval cost.

Why it matters: Structuring memory retrieval as local stateful traversal rather than stateless global search can significantly improve training efficiency and reduce computational overhead in long-context agents.

entry.title: EpiAgent: Epistemic Self-Play for LLM Agents
entry.summary:
EpiAgent introduces a learnable epistemic layer for LLM agents that maintains explicit beliefs about private information and optimizes policy and belief updates through Epistemic Self-Play using bi-level optimization.

Why it matters: Equipping LLM agents with explicit, learnable belief-updating mechanisms improves strategic decision-making and performance in complex multi-agent interactions with incomplete information.

entry.title: Composing and Steering Diffusion Models with Generalized Feynman-Kac Correctors
entry.summary:
Generalized Feynman-Kac correctors (GFKC) enable exact zero-shot sampling and reward-based steering from arbitrary compositions of pretrained diffusion models by solving a Feynman-Kac partial differential equation in the log domain without retraining.

Why it matters: It allows complex compositions and reward-guided control of multiple pretrained diffusion models without requiring model retraining, fine-tuning, or heuristic score combination approximations.

entry.title: Factorized Representations of Concurrent Temporal Variables in Pretrained Language Models
entry.summary:
Pretrained language models represent multiple independently evolving temporal variables via approximately factorized, linearly decodable, and additive joint-state geometry in overlapping hidden-state subspaces.

Why it matters: Understanding how language models isolate concurrent context variables into approximately additive, selectively accessible subspaces helps elucidate the internal mechanisms of multi-track contextual tracking.

entry.title: ShallowDefend: Harnessing Shallow Safety Alignment for Multi-Turn Defender
entry.summary:
ShallowDefend introduces an Assess-Decide-Respond framework that uses reinforcement learning at the payload turn to force models to generate an explicit, parseable safety decision token span before generating a multi-turn response.

Why it matters: It converts the inherent shallow token vulnerability exploited by multi-turn jailbreaks into an efficient, rule-verifiable defense mechanism that achieves superior multi-turn safety with minimal impact on model utility.

entry.title: PIVOT: Progressive Intervention via Online Teacher Correction
entry.summary:
PIVOT combines trajectory-level interventions with token-level KL supervision by inserting teacher-generated corrections directly into student rollouts during online reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR).

Why it matters: PIVOT enables language models to learn complex logic and mathematical reasoning tasks where standard RLVR fails due to extremely sparse rewards.

entry.title: Every Token Needs Its Own Teacher: Multi-teacher Adaptive On-policy Self-distillation
entry.summary:
MTA-OPSD introduces token-level adaptive selection from a multi-teacher pool for on-policy self-distillation, allowing every token to select its preferred teacher dynamically during training.

Why it matters: Adapting teacher supervision at the individual token level significantly improves the performance of large language models during post-training self-distillation.

entry.title: Incentivizing Self-Learning in Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
A reinforcement learning approach using a custom interface incentivizes LLMs to autonomously acquire, process, and apply knowledge from long-form textbooks to solve complex mathematical problems.

Why it matters: Reinforcement learning over autonomous reference navigation allows LLMs to handle unfamiliar domains and long-context problem solving without relying on preassembled contexts or static retrieval.

entry.title: Raincheck: Deferred Multimodal Prefill for Efficient Multi-Turn MLLM Inference
entry.summary:
Raincheck introduces deferred multimodal prefill for MLLMs, progressively processing pruned visual tokens during idle decode capacity and scheduling gaps to restore multi-turn accuracy without increasing TTFT.

Why it matters: It enables MLLMs to achieve the low initial latency of aggressively pruned prefill while recovering lost accuracy for subsequent conversation turns at virtually no TPOT overhead.

entry.title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching
entry.summary:
Intrinsic Distribution Matching (IDM) enhances diffusion distillation by combining reverse-KL score matching with explicit moment constraints on feature means and standard deviations computed from the generator's EMA copy.

Why it matters: IDM achieves state-of-the-art text rendering performance on LongText-Bench at two network function evaluations without requiring auxiliary external encoders.

entry.title: A-RSI: Adaptive Task Refresh for Zero-Data Multimodal Self-Improvement
entry.summary:
A-RSI enables zero-data multimodal self-improvement by using training dynamics to adaptively refresh a pool of programmatically generated tasks without external data or test-set access.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that vision-language models can continuously self-improve without human labels, external datasets, or validation leakages by algorithmically managing their own task refresh cycles.

entry.title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs
entry.summary:
LOWN is a training-free decoding method for Diffusion Vision-Language Models that reduces FLOPs by skipping visual token processing whenever image-free predictions match previous image-conditioned outputs.

Why it matters: It drastically cuts inference computational overhead in diffusion VLMs without requiring model retraining, fine-tuning, or performance tradeoffs.

entry.title: L3G-World: Real-Time Infinite World Generation with Latent 3D Gaussian Memory
entry.summary:
L3G-World enables real-time 9 FPS infinite world generation using a Latent 3D Gaussian Memory that updates with scene extent rather than stream length.

Why it matters: By removing VAE re-encoding bottlenecks and decoupling memory growth from stream length, the architecture achieves 9 FPS real-time generation of spatially consistent, long-horizon interactive 3D environments.

entry.title: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training
entry.summary:
WorkFactory is a scalable framework that uses information support graphs and probe executions to construct 112,686 executable professional tasks across 612 occupations for training working agents.

Why it matters: It provides an automated methodology to fix defective task environments and generate massive, reliable demonstration datasets for training AI agents on complex real-world occupations.

entry.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
entry.summary:
SpecSlot is a pixel-space rectified-flow Transformer that decouples spectral detail from global attention sequence length by expanding spatial anchors into frequency-specific slots that interact locally.

Why it matters: It enables generative Transformers to scale up fine-grained spatial and spectral visual details without incurring the quadratic computational costs of long global attention sequences.

entry.title: Co-Design Bench: Multimodal Collaborative Coding Evaluation for Agentic Models
entry.summary:
Co-Design Bench is a reference-free benchmark containing 273 multimodal tasks and 2,331 hidden criteria to evaluate agentic models on real-user application editing.

Why it matters: It establishes a realistic, execution-based standard for evaluating how effectively AI agents convert complex multimodal user feedback into fully functional codebases.

entry.title: HairDeck: Animation-Ready Stylized Hair Cards from a Single Image
entry.summary:
HairDeck is a set diffusion transformer that generates animation-ready stylized hair cards and spring-bone chains from a single image.

Why it matters: It enables rapid creation of fully animatable stylized 3D character hair assets from a single input image for games and avatars.

entry.title: WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One Agent From Narration to Long-Form Video
entry.summary:
WeVisCut introduces a 9B single-agent policy and harness for long-form script-to-video editing that matches Claude Opus 5 performance while using 33x fewer generated tokens per successful output minute.

Why it matters: It proves that a compact, task-adapted 9B model can achieve frontier-level video editing quality at a fraction of the computational and token cost of large generalist LLMs.

entry.title: IntReal: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Multimodal Interleaved Generation
entry.summary:
IntReal introduces IntReal-100K, a real-world multimodal interleaved dataset, along with a fine-grained, seven-dimension evaluation suite that achieves strong human agreement and low redundancy for benchmarking Unified Multimodal Models.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized benchmark for interleaved generation and demonstrates that models can be improved via modality-specific optimization rather than relying strictly on joint text-image training.

entry.title: PhysInsert: Physically Plausible Object Insertion with Geometric Priors and Bidirectional Object-Scene Interactions
entry.summary:
PhysInsert is a framework for physically plausible object insertion that utilizes VGGT geometry streams and 2D spatial supervision to jointly adapt object pose, illumination, and scene interactions using a novel Blender-rendered dataset.

Why it matters: It enables more realistic synthetic image editing and composition by ensuring inserted objects automatically match the perspective, pose, and lighting of the target environment.

entry.title: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments
entry.summary:
WebAnything is a fully automated framework that reconstructs source-grounded, reusable web environments from real URLs using an Explorer-Builder and an independent verifier, eliminating per-site manual setup and repairs.

Why it matters: It enables scalable, reproducible training and evaluation of web agents by automatically converting real-world websites into executable environments without manual engineering.

entry.title: Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker
entry.summary:
Glance unifies reranking and generation into a single resident 9B model using a lightweight decision adapter and pointer head to score candidate passages from a shared prefill.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need to host and run separate models for reranking and generation in RAG pipelines, significantly reducing latency, GPU memory overhead, and redundant processing.

entry.title: AskStream: When and What to Ask Proactively under Uncertainty in Streaming Video Understanding
entry.summary:
AskStream is a streaming video benchmark introducing an 'ask' action to help multimodal models actively request missing information under video or user uncertainty.

Why it matters: It establishes a standard for evaluating proactive agents that must clarify ambiguous user queries or incomplete video inputs instead of waiting indefinitely or hallucinating responses.

entry.title: EditAgent: Rethinking Agentic Image Editing
entry.summary:
EditAgent improves agentic image editing by expanding the action space with specialized tools and enhancing the observation space with structured verification records for parallel listwise judging.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that combining specialized tool routing with parallel candidate verification significantly cuts compute costs and improves quality over traditional sequential refinement in vision-language tasks.

entry.title: Rethinking Neural Thickets Without Weight Perturbations
entry.summary:
Researchers debunk the Neural Thickets weight-geometry hypothesis, demonstrating that its gains stem from output diversity, validation-based selection, and voting, which can be matched using a training-free logit perturbation method called PSV.

Why it matters: Logit PSV provides a simple, computation-light, training-free alternative to weight-perturbation ensembles across language and vision models without requiring model weight modifications.

entry.title: SCARL: Sequence Confidence-Aligned Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
SCARL reshapes reinforcement learning advantages using sequence-confidence alignment gaps, preventing entropy collapse and improving language-model reasoning without requiring extra forward/backward passes.

Why it matters: SCARL enhances policy optimization in verifiable reasoning tasks by preventing premature entropy collapse and better separating correct from incorrect responses across diverse RL estimators.

entry.title: How to Loop Your Transformer: Loop Scaling, Specialization, and Parallel Inference
entry.summary:
A comprehensive study on dense decoder-only transformers reveals that looping strategies must align with parameter or training FLOP constraints, and introduces adapter specialization and modified parallel looping to improve quality and inference speed.

Why it matters: Designing looped transformers according to specific compute constraints and architecture modifications allows practitioners to scale model depth and inference throughput without increasing parameter counts.

entry.title: Distributional Reward Calibration and Budget-Neutral Credit Assignment for Multimodal RLVR
entry.summary:
TACE improves GRPO advantage estimation through optimal-transport reward standardization and budget-neutral token credit assignment.

Why it matters: TACE prevents heavy-tailed reward outliers and unconstrained token updates from destabilizing reinforcement learning from verifier rewards (RLVR) in multimodal models.

entry.title: An ODE-based Sampler for Discrete Diffusion Models
entry.summary:
Exponential residual flows (ERFs) introduce a deterministic, ODE-based sampling framework for discrete diffusion models by augmenting discrete tokens with continuous residual variables.

Why it matters: It enables deterministic probability flow sampling and consistency distillation in discrete diffusion models, leading to faster sampling and improved performance in text and code generation.

entry.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
entry.summary:
A unified framework replaces the multi-stage training pipeline by deriving RL objectives as maximum-likelihood fitting to model-generated target distributions, training foundation models with a single likelihood-based algorithm.

Why it matters: It simplifies the foundation model post-training infrastructure and improves compute efficiency by replacing disparate training algorithms with a single likelihood-based system.

entry.title: Preserving Utility in Continual LLM Unlearning via Orthogonal Projections
entry.summary:
Continual Orthogonal Projection (COP) prevents model degradation during sequential LLM unlearning by restricting gradient updates to the orthogonal complement of low-rank activation subspaces cached from previous forget sets.

Why it matters: COP enables long-term compliance with data removal requests (such as privacy or copyright enforcement) in deployed LLMs without causing performance collapse or requiring costly retraining from scratch.

entry.title: Latent Path Exploration via Potential-Guided Subtrajectory Balance
entry.summary:
SubLAT improves stochastic continuous latent reasoning in language models by coupling a relative answer potential with Subtrajectory Balance to guide intermediate transition paths.

Why it matters: It enables language models to effectively explore complex, multi-path reasoning spaces in continuous latent representations without producing explicit token traces.

entry.title: Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution
entry.summary:
The CATT benchmark isolates LM data attribution failures, revealing that negative log-odds gradients and top-token aggregation significantly improve attribution recall over standard document-averaging cross-entropy methods.

Why it matters: Simple changes to loss gradient formulation and token aggregation can dramatically improve the accuracy of tracing specific outputs back to training data without inventing new estimators.

entry.title: Multi-View MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation
entry.summary:
Multi-View MoE uses multiple independent routers to aggregate expert scores and dynamically mix latent input views for expert computation without increasing the active-expert budget.

Why it matters: It improves MoE routing accuracy and downstream performance at zero additional FLOP or communication cost per active expert.
